flashcard_questions.q: What is the weather gauge in a sailing battle?
flashcard_questions.a: The upwind position, which lets a fleet choose when to engage.

flashcard_questions.q: Which port did the English fleet sail from to meet the Armada?
On what date was the Armada first sighted off Cornwall?
How did the English coast supply Howard’s ships during the Channel fight?
flashcard_questions.a: Every port on that coast was English, so they could restock.

flashcard_questions.q: Why could the Armada not restock during the Channel fight?
flashcard_questions.a: It had no friendly quay between Spain and the Netherlands.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a roadstead in navigation?
flashcard_questions.a: An open stretch of water where ships anchor without the shelter of a harbour.

flashcard_questions.q: Why did the Armada anchor off Calais rather than in a harbour?
flashcard_questions.a: Spain controlled no deep-water port on that coast.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Dutch ships blockaded Parma’s barges behind the sandbanks?
What lasting damage did cutting their cables do to the Spanish ships?
flashcard_questions.a: They sailed the rest of the campaign without their best anchors.

flashcard_questions.q: On what date did the English close to gunnery range off Gravelines?
Which sandbanks nearly wrecked the damaged Armada after Gravelines?
Which route home was the Armada forced to take?
flashcard_questions.a: North around Scotland and west around Ireland.

flashcard_questions.q: Roughly what share of the Armada’s ships never returned to Spain?
Why is the “God blew” medal only partly true?
flashcard_questions.a: English action had already driven the fleet onto the northern route.

notes: 14 cards: 5 term-to-definition from the site glossary, 4 cause-effect (feature to consequence), 3 event/date, 2 figure. Skipped the 'four environments' framing as it would be a list answer.
